description: Welcome to Team SESHAT! Formed specifically for this 48-hour challenge, we are building a brand-new decision-support tool from scratch. We fuse ancient Egyptian wisdom with NASA data (SMAP, ECOSTRESS). Over this weekend, we will code our "GEB Map" UI and integrate our "HAPY" hardware concept. By Sunday, we aim to deliver the "PERET Cycle" AI for smart crop rotations. We are translating cosmic data into earthly survival. Watch us build a global AgriTech solution live!
summary: SESHAT is an advanced decision-support platform designed for Egyptian farmers to tackle climate change, soil degradation, and water scarcity under the NASA Space Apps "Field Shift" challenge. By fusing multi-satellite Earth observations—including NASA SMAP for soil moisture, ECOSTRESS for land surface temperature, GPM for precipitation, and ESA Sentinel-2 for vegetation health (NDVI)—with the HAPY IoT ground sensor, SESHAT translates complex space data into actionable, farmer-friendly insights. The platform evaluates three distinct crop rotation strategies (Existing, Water-Conservation, and Soil-Restoration) using the 33% Sweet Spot algorithm. SESHAT empowers farmers to optimize irrigation, restore soil fertility, and secure sustainable agricultural productivity without replacing human expertise.
details:
• What It Does & How It Works: " SESHAT X " is an end-to-end precision agriculture and irrigation decision-support platform built for arid and desert reclamation zones (such as Toshka, East Owainat, New Valley, and the Nile Delta). It fuses multi-orbital satellite observations (Sentinel-2 optical bands,Sentinel-1 Radar, NASA MODIS LST & ET, NASA SMAP soil moisture, and Landsat 8/9) with micro-climate telemetry (ERA5-Land, OpenWeatherMap) and edge IoT data from Hapy-60 (CM-60) center-pivot controllers. Our analytics engine runs FAO-56 Penman-Monteith crop water balance models (ETc), computes the Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index (TVDI), and uses a CatBoost ML classifier (catboost_crop_health.cbm) to detect water and heat stress 48–72 hours before visible canopy wilting, alongside spatial NDVI Coefficient of Variation (CV) and rule-based telemetry diagnostics to catch mechanical/electrical pivot tower faults early.
  • Benefits & Intended Impact: Prevents groundwater aquifer depletion in desert farms, reduces diesel and electricity pumping costs by prescribing exact daily pump runtimes (m3/ha), prevents sudden crop collapse under extreme desert heat (>40o C), and empowers farmers to compare resilient crop rotation strategies without needing expensive in-situ flux towers.
  • Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software:

- Languages: Python (49.5%), TypeScript (49.2%), CSS, HTML, Shell/PowerShell.

- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript 5.8+, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, bilingual RTL/LTR interface (Arabic/English).
- Backend & Security: Flask 3.0.3, SQLite (WAL mode) with multi-tenant isolation, AES-256 (Fernet) encryption, APScheduler, Gunicorn/Nginx.
- AI, ML & Remote Sensing: Google Earth Engine (GEE) API, NumPy, CatBoost 1.2+, local RAG agronomic assistant powered by Ollama (qwen2.5:3b), and FAO-56 agronomy physics.
- Hardware & Messaging: Hapy-60 pivot telemetry edge sensors (voltage, current, PSI pressure, speed) and multi-channel alerts via WhatsApp (Twilio), Telegram, SMTP, and automated PDF/Excel bulletins.

  • Creativity & Factors Considered: Overcomes the "lagging indicator trap" of optical NDVI by combining thermal and L-band microwave data. Engineered specifically for harsh 2G/3G desert connectivity using asynchronous background jobs (HTTP 202), ETag/304 caching, idempotency keys, E.164 Egyptian phone normalization, and ancient Egyptian cultural storytelling (Seshat, Hapy, GEB , Peret).
